title: decade list spins the CPU until the server answers
body:
`control::list` connects a blocking `UnixStream`, pushes `ViewerMessage::List`, then loops on `decoder.next_server_message()` and `decoder.receive(&stream)`. `Decoder::receive` in `wire.rs` receives with `RECEIVE_FLAGS`, which include `DONTWAIT`, and maps `EAGAIN` to `Ok(true)`. So the loop in `list` never blocks and burns a core until the listing arrives.

`script.rs` polls the socket with `rustix::event::poll` before each receive, and `State::close_viewers` in `compositor.rs` has a third hand-written poll loop with a deadline. `UnixStream::connect(viewer_socket_path()).map_err(|_| "no server is running")` is written in both `control.rs` and `script.rs`. In `script.rs`, `while !outbox.is_empty() { if !send { break } }` does what one `send` call does.

## Proposal

One wait helper in `wire.rs`, something like `Decoder::wait(&stream, timeout)` and `Outbox::flush(&stream, deadline)`, used by `list`, `script` and `close_viewers`. A `control::connect()` replaces the two connect copies.
close_reason: Fixed in 03425fe. Decoder::wait and Outbox::flush in wire.rs poll before they read or send. control::list, the script pump and State::close_viewers use them, and control::connect replaces the two connect copies. A control.rs test checks the CPU time spent waiting for a listing.
